content.title: About
content.content: Multigrain bread is a whole‑grain loaf made from a blend of different cereals, seeds, and sometimes nuts. It has a dense crumb, a nutty‑seed aroma, and higher fiber and nutrient content compared with regular white bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix can include wheat, rye, barley, oats, sunflower, pumpkin and flax seeds.
Multigrain bread often contains more B‑vitamins and minerals such as iron and magnesium.
Flax seeds add a source of omega‑3 fatty acids.
Traditionally it is baked in stone ovens, giving the crust a crisp, crunchy texture.
Many countries have their own versions, e.g., Scandinavian “rød” or Italian “pan di campani”.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: High dietary fiber improves digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide a steadier blood‑sugar level than white bread.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2, B3 and folate support energy metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Minerals and antioxidants
items.content: Magnesium, iron, zinc and seed antioxidants help boost immunity and bone health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Whole grains give the loaf a lower GI, which is beneficial for weight management.

items.title: Allergy to grain or seeds
items.content: Some individuals may react to wheat, rye or seeds such as sunflower or pumpkin.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid this bread.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Certain varieties may contain added salt or preservatives; choose a plain, additive‑free version when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Multigrain bread works well for toast, sandwiches, and as a side for soups and salads. Toast it, spread avocado, cottage cheese or hummus, or pair with cheese, ham and vegetable fillings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the loaf in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag – it stays fresh for up to 2 months. Thaw in the oven or toaster before use.
